As per prosecution story the mother of the victim presented herself with a written application on 12.12.2021 at 3:00 PM that she was cleaning utensils at home and her daughter was playing near a mango tree.
In the meanwhile her daughter came to her weeping and told that the accused - Vikas called her and offered her money.
When she went to him the accused took the victim in a hut and threw away her underwear after he pulled it off and started entering his penis in vagina of the victim.
The victim felt pain and started weeping.
In the meanwhile accused-Vikas ran way.
On the written application of mother of the victim, Nalishi No.130 of 2021 was registered and later it was registered as Crime No.685 of 2021.
3. After completing necessary formalities and investigation charge-sheet was filed against appellant.
When appellant was charged for offences under Sections 376, 376   of IPC and under Section 5/6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act 2012, he denied the same.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: After prosecution evidence in his examination under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. he pleaded innocence and denied prosecution evidence but did not lead any defence evidence.
4. Learned trial Court vide impugned judgment has convicted and sentenced the appellant for offense as has been stated hereinabove.
5. Learned counsel for the appellant challenging the impugned judgment urged that prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
There are material contradictions and omission in the prosecution evidence.
No independent witness has supported the prosecution case.
He further submits that the appellant has been falsely implicated due to animosity of water irrigation regarding agricultural land between parents of prosecutrix and accused.
PW-5 who is represented in the case as sole eye-witness of the case has not supported the prosecution story.
PW-1 the prosecutrix is a tutored witness.
The medical evidence has not supported the case of the prosecution.
Medical evidence indicate that there is no external injury on the body of victim and only there was mild swelling in Vulva.
Hence, judgment of the learned trial Court convicting and sentencing the appellant deserves to be set aside and appellant is liable to be acquitted.

6. On the other hand, learned Government Advocate has supported the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:55156 3 CRA-10170-2023 impugned judgment and prayed for dismissal of instant appeal.

sentences.text: We have perused the record as also impugned judgment of the learned trial Court and considered the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the rival parties.
the prosecutrix has stated that the accused took off her underwear.
When she was asked in para-1 of examination-in-chief whether the accused did anything else with her then this witness nodded her head in negative.
Again she was asked for the second time whether the accused besides pulling her underwear did anything else, she again answered in negative.

At this stage, the prosecution sought permission to ask a leading question which was given by the trial court in which she supported statements under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. (Ex.P- 1) in which details of offence have been given as per prosecution case.
In para-4 of cross-examination she stated that it is true that on the question of irrigating the field there was fight between her father and Suresh Bharti.
Her mother had told what to state in the court.
She has deposed in the court as informed by her mother.
9. PW-2 mother of the victim stated that she was washing utensils at home and her daughter was playing near a mango tree.
In the meanwhile her daughter came to her weeping and told that the accused - Vikas called her and offered her money and when she went with him.
Then the accused took the victim in a hut and threw away her underwear after pulling it off and started entering his penis in vagina of the victim.
In cross-examination she denied that she is speaking against the appellant accused because of some dispute.
10. PW-3 father of the victim stated that the incident is of 12 th December 2021.
He was available in his vegetable shop at the time of incident.
When he had gone to take meal in front of his shop, he had received a phone call of his wife who had narrated the incident.
When he enquired from the accused he refused the allegation and stated that he had only pulled off underwear of the victim.
PW-3 and his wife PW-2 both had given consent for medical examination of the victim.
In para-14 of cross-examination PW-3 denied that there was dispute with the accused and his family regarding irrigation of field.
11. PW-4 stated that the victim is his niece.

He stated that parents of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:55156 4 CRA-10170-2023 victim had engaged the accused for irrigation purpose and to look after the fields.
He stated that he does not know whether there was any dispute regarding water irrigation between father of the victim and the accused.
Uncle of the prosecutrix in para-7 of cross-examination denied this suggestion that due to irrigating field the appellant has been falsely implicated by the complainant party.
12. PW-5 the prosecutrix's friend identified the accused who had appeared through video conferencing but she stated that she does not know his name.
She stated that she does study in L.KG.
PW-5 did not support the case of the prosecution and turned hostile.
PW-5 friend of the prosecutrix who is about seven years of age was asked a leading question by the prosecution.
In para-2 she did not support the prosecution case.

sentences.text: Dr. Meenakshi Mishra stated that on conducting the internal medical examination of prosecutrix she found mild swelling on Vulva of the prosecutrix.
PW-9 Dr. Meenakshi Mishra in para-3 of her cross-examination stated that in Ex.P-9 she has not mentioned cause of swelling in the report.
There is disease namely vulvitis in the girls child and women in which there is itching on infection on Vulva region.
14. PW-10 Manisha Upadhyay has stated date of birth of prosecutrix is 18.3.2017.
She stated that she had seized the birth certificate of the prosecutrix by seizure memo Ex.P-6.
It is seen that seizure memo of birth certificate is exhibited but no birth certificate is available on record which could be primary evidence.
In para-20 PW-10 has stated that she did not investigate whether there was any animosity between the complainant and the accused family on the ground of irrigating the fields.

15. When entire oral and documentary evidence is considered we find that the case against the appellant is found proved that he had taken the victim in a hut and by pulling off her underwear violated the privacy of the victim and thus committed sexual assault.

16. Section 7 and 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act read as under:-
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55156 5 CRA-10170-2023 7. Sexual assault.-- Whoever, with sexual intent touches the vagina, penis, anus or breast of the child or makes the child touch the vagina, penis, anus or breast of such person or any other person, or does any other act with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration is said to commit sexual assault.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 8. Punishment for sexual assault .--Whoever, commits sexual assault, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.

17. On overall consideration of the case it is found that the only evidence which can be considered by this court is regarding taking off underwear of the victim by the accused and there is no evidence regarding violation of her privacy.
Thus, the case of the appellant will fall under Sections 363 of IPC and Section 7 and 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act 2012.

Therefore conviction and sentence under Sections 376, 376   of IPC and Section 5/6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act 2012 is set aside and the appellant is convicted and sentenced under Section 363 of IPC and under Sections 7 and 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act 2012 for a period 4 years R.I. each from the date of his arrest and fine of Rs.1000/-
with default stipulation of 06 months R.I.

19. The disposal of the case property shall be done as per judgment of the trial court.
